chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first, 'How did the washing for the day of Friday come to be an Obligation?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Blessed and High, Completed the Obligatory Salat with the optional Salat, and Completed the Obligatory Fasting with the optional Fasting, and Completed the Obligatory Wudu with the washing of the day of Friday, [covering] whatever was during that from the mistake, or shortening, or forgetfulness, or deficiency'.
ai.seo_question: Why is the Friday Ghusl considered obligatory in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Al-Husayn ibn Khalid inquires of Imam Al-Reza (AS) regarding the obligatory status of Friday Ghusl. The Imam elucidates that Friday Ghusl serves to perfect the obligatory Wudu, analogous to how voluntary acts complete obligatory ones, thereby rectifying any minor deficiencies, forgetfulness, or shortcomings in the basic ablution. This establishes the theological principle that ritual purity is a cumulative process where supererogatory acts enhance the validity of core obligations.
